Chapter 7: Building a Career—Challenges, Breakthroughs, and the Value of Persistence.
Making the leap from school to the working world is tough for just about anyone. But if you’re someone who thinks in pictures and feels everything deeply, that leap can feel more like stepping straight into the unknown. Suddenly, the rules aren’t written down anywhere, and it’s hard to know exactly what people expect from you. Even the job interviews can feel like a minefield—questions popping up that seem designed to trip you up, and then there’s the confusing dance of small talk and office politics.
After college, she sets out to find her place in animal science. And those first days? They’re rough. Some employers don’t really get her way of thinking, doubting whether she can handle the job. Others might not know what to make of her honesty or the fact that she sometimes misses social cues. There are plenty of moments where rejection stings and disappointment settles in—times when giving up almost seems easier.
But here’s where persistence really comes in. She doesn’t back down. Instead, she learns to speak up for herself, to share her strengths, and to ask for the support she needs. Along the way, she finds people who see her value—supervisors who appreciate her incredible attention to detail, coworkers who genuinely respect her straightforwardness. Little by little, she builds a reputation for excellence. People start to notice her creative designs and her deep understanding of animal behavior.
Then comes a real breakthrough. She’s asked to redesign a livestock facility. Now, instead of just following the usual blueprint, she visualizes the whole space—walking through it in her mind, picturing how the animals will react and move. With her sketches and detailed diagrams, her vision comes alive. And when the facility is finished, it’s a hit. People praise how efficient it is, but also how much better it is for the animals.
Of course, things aren’t always smooth. There are setbacks—projects that don’t pan out, misunderstandings with coworkers, moments when doubt starts to creep in. But each time a challenge comes up, she meets it with determination and a fresh burst of creativity. She learns to navigate all those unwritten social rules, even developing little scripts for everyday interactions and finding smart ways to handle sensory overload.
What really stands out is this: success isn’t just about talent or being smart. It’s about resilience, the ability to adapt, and having the guts to keep pushing forward—even when the odds seem stacked against you. If you think differently, your journey might be tougher. But the rewards? They’re just as real—and maybe even sweeter.
